events.text: Wikipedia goes online as a single English-language edition
Jeff Bezos founds Amazon as an online bookshop
Three former PayPal employees found YouTube
Larry Page and Sergey Brin found Google

reveal.explanation: Amazon started as an online bookshop in 1994 and Google followed four years later as a search engine set up by two computer scientists. Wikipedia went online in January 2001 and YouTube in 2005, by which time much of everyday life had moved onto the web.

sources.excerpt: On July 5, 1994, Amazon was founded as "Cadabra" by Jeff Bezos, after he relocated from New York City to Bellevue, Washington, to operate an online bookstore.
Google was founded in 1998 by American computer scientists Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

Wikipedia was launched on January 15, 2001 (sometimes referred to as "Wikipedia Day"), as a single English language edition with the domain name www.wikipedia.com, and was announced by Sanger on the Nupedia mailing list.
YouTube was founded on February 14, 2005, by Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim, and Steve Chen who were all former employees at PayPal.

editorNotes: Amazon was founded as Cadabra in July 1994 and renamed Amazon that November, so the year is the same either way. Google began as a research project in January 1996 but the article dates the founding of the company to 1998, which is used. Wikipedia is dated by its 15 January 2001 launch rather than Sanger's proposal five days earlier; YouTube by its 14 February 2005 founding rather than the first upload that April.
